title: Vietnam draft lottery as IV for military service on earnings

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy  
Method: Two-Stage Least Squares (IV).  
Justification: Draft-lottery numbers were randomly assigned, satisfy independence; low numbers raised the probability of serving ⇒ strong relevance; the lottery number should affect later earnings only through military service ⇒ exclusion restriction.  
Key assumptions:  
• Relevance: Cov(z,x) ≠ 0 (first-stage F-stat > 10).  
• Exclusion: Draft number affects earnings only via veteran status.  
• Independence/Random assignment: z ⟂ potential earnings.  
• Monotonicity: Nobody serves less because they got a low number.  

## 2. R Code
```r
############################################################
# Vietnam draft lottery IV: effect of veteran status on earnings
# File path supplied in the prompt.
############################################################

# install.packages("AER")   # uncomment if not installed
library(AER)
library(sandwich)
library(lmtest)

# 1. Read the data ----------------------------------------------------------
dat <- read.csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s21_data.csv")

# quick check
print(head(dat))

#------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Baseline 2SLS: instrument 'x' (veteran) with 'z' (low draft number)
#------------------------------------------------------------------------------

iv_baseline <- ivreg(y ~ x + controls | z + controls, data = dat)
coeftest(iv_baseline, vcov = vcovHC(iv_baseline, type = "HC1"))[ "x", ]

#------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Diagnostics & robustness
#------------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 3.1 First-stage strength
first_stage <- lm(x ~ z + controls, data = dat)
fs_res <- coeftest(first_stage, vcov = vcovHC(first_stage, type = "HC1"))
fstat <- linearHypothesis(first_stage, "z = 0", vcov = vcovHC(first_stage, type = "HC1"))$F[2]
cat("\nFirst-stage coefficient on z and robust F-stat:\n")
print(fs_res["z", ])
cat("Robust F-statistic on instrument =", round(fstat, 2), "\n")

## 3.2 Reduced-form (intention to treat)
rf <- lm(y ~ z + controls, data = dat)
cat("\nReduced-form effect of lottery on earnings:\n")
print(coeftest(rf, vcov = vcovHC(rf, "HC1"))["z", ])

## 3.3 Naïve OLS for comparison
ols <- lm(y ~ x + controls, data = dat)
cat("\nNaïve OLS estimate:\n")
print(coeftest(ols, vcov = vcovHC(ols, "HC1"))["x", ])

## 3.4 Alternative instrument specification: numeric draft number
#       (lower numbers are stronger inducement; use z_num = 365 - raw number)
if(!"z_num" %in% names(dat)){
  dat$z_num <- 365 - dat$z_raw   # only if original raw number existed
}

# If z is already binary, skip; otherwise run
if("z_num" %in% names(dat)){
  iv_alt <- ivreg(y ~ x + controls | z_num + controls, data = dat)
  cat("\nAlternative IV (numeric draft number) estimate:\n")
  print(coeftest(iv_alt, vcov = vcovHC(iv_alt, "HC1"))["x", ])
}

############################################################
# End of script
############################################################
```

The script prints:  
• 2SLS coefficient on veteran status with robust SE and p-value  
• First-stage coefficient and robust F-statistic  
• Reduced-form and naïve OLS coefficients  
• Alternative instrument estimate (if numeric lottery number exists)  

## 3. Expected Findings  
Direction: negative – Vietnam-era military service lowered long-run log earnings.  
Magnitude: roughly −0.10 to −0.15 (≈10–15 % reduction).  
Rationale: prior studies (e.g., Angrist 1990) find ~15 % earnings penalty; conscription pulled men from civilian labor force, delayed education/experience and carried psychological/health costs.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: IV/2SLS — instrument: draft lottery number; LATE for compliers (drafted but wouldn't have volunteered)
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Military service reduces earnings for complier veterans
